Key poses for athletic performance (hold 30–60 sec each):

  • Downward Dog — stretches hamstrings and calves
  • Pigeon Pose — releases hip flexors
  • Warrior II — builds hip strength and balance
  • Bridge Pose — activates glutes and spine
  • Seated Forward Fold — deep hamstring release

Practice 3–4x per week to reduce injury risk and accelerate recovery.

10-minute morning sequence:

  1. Cat-Cow — 1 min
  2. Hip circles — 1 min each side
  3. World's Greatest Stretch — 2 min each side
  4. Thoracic rotation — 1 min each side
  5. Standing hamstring reach — 2 min

Key tip: Move slowly and with intention. Daily practice improves posture, reduces pain, and boosts energy.

Pre-workout (1–2 hrs before): Eat complex carbs + moderate protein. Try oats with banana or rice with chicken.

Post-workout (within 30–60 min): Prioritize protein for muscle repair and fast carbs to replenish glycogen. Ideal: protein shake + fruit.

Hydration: Drink 500ml of water before training and sip throughout your session.

5 quick muscle-building meals under 15 minutes:

  1. Greek yogurt parfait — 30g protein
  2. Chicken & rice bowl with veggies — 45g protein
  3. Tuna avocado wrap — 35g protein
  4. Egg white omelette with cottage cheese — 28g protein
  5. Protein shake with oats and banana — 40g protein

Dedicate 2 hours every Sunday to transform your week:

  1. Cook a large batch of protein (chicken, eggs, or tofu)
  2. Prepare 2–3 complex carbs (rice, sweet potato, quinoa)
  3. Roast a variety of vegetables
  4. Portion into containers for 5 days

Key tip: Store proteins and carbs separately to maintain freshness and flexibility when building meals.

Jump rope burns up to 15 calories per minute. Start with the basic two-foot bounce: 30 seconds on, 30 seconds rest for 10 rounds.

Progression: Alternate feet for coordination, then advance to double-unders (rope passes twice per jump).

Key tip: Always land softly on the balls of your feet to protect your joints.

Position the bar across your upper traps. Stand feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out. Break at the hips and knees simultaneously, sit back and down until thighs are parallel to the floor.

Sets & Reps: 4 sets of 6–8 reps.

Key tip: Prioritize depth over load — proper squat depth recruits glutes, quads, and hamstrings fully.

The deadlift is the king of compound movements. Stand with feet hip-width, grip the bar just outside your legs. Hinge at the hips, engage your core, and drive through your heels to stand.

Sets & Reps: 3 sets of 5–6 reps for strength.

Key tip: Keep your spine neutral throughout — never round your lower back under load.

Start with the run/walk method and build week by week:

  • Week 1: Run 1 min, walk 2 min — repeat 8x
  • Week 2: Run 2 min, walk 2 min — repeat 6x
  • Week 4: Run 5 min, walk 1 min — repeat 4x

Key tip: Run at a conversational pace — you should be able to talk while moving.

This workout alternates 40 seconds of effort with 20 seconds of rest. Complete 3 rounds of: Jump squats, Burpees, Mountain climbers, High knees, Push-ups, Lateral shuffles.

Total time: ~30 minutes.

Key tip: Keep intensity maximal during work intervals. No equipment needed — just bring the effort.

The bench press targets your chest, shoulders, and triceps. Lie flat, grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width. Lower the bar to mid-chest and press back up with control.

Sets & Reps: 3–4 sets of 8–12 reps.

Key tips: Keep your feet flat on the floor, avoid bouncing the bar, and maintain a slight arch in your lower back.
